A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same mTSBench work and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering, with no material reading gaps.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 24 anomaly detectors and three model selectors on 344 time series, including performance, ranking, runtime, and anomaly-length analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, stratified analyses, ranking curves, and qualitative prediction case studies.

M1.justification: The detector pool, three model-selection algorithms, and documented adaptations remain unchanged. V1 Appendices C/E correspond to v2 Appendices D/F. The added PCA and Ensemble comparisons are evaluation baselines, without a revision to the benchmark's existing algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 344 time series from 19 datasets. New subgroup analyses and case studies reuse this coverage. Revised PSM and SWAN-SF descriptions and domain labels do not establish replacement of the evaluated data.

E2.justification: V2 adds fixed-choice PCA and an Ensemble averaging all 24 detectors' anomaly scores to the model-selection comparison in Table 2. PCA previously appeared as a detector, but not as a comparator in this table. The three selectors and Oracle, Near-optimal, and Random baselines remain.

E3.justification: Table 2 expands from 12 to 13 metrics by separating F1 from Max-F1; the earlier F1 entries are retained under Max-F1. V2 also adds ranking-depth and stratified evaluations. The short-anomaly cutoff changes from fewer than 2 points in v1 Appendix D to fewer than 20 in v2 Appendix E, although the corresponding heatmap retains its entries; rerunning is not established.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands analysis of selector failure conditions: Tables 3–5 examine anomaly ratio, anomaly duration, and application domain, while Figure 6 examines ranking depth. New Appendix C compares annotation salience and detector predictions on selected series. The earlier dimensionality and extreme-anomaly-length analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across evaluated time series. The additional grouped tables extend that reporting practice without introducing repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results for the new baselines, subgroup analyses, ranking curves, case studies, and dataset-specific detector runtimes. Table 2 reports PCA AUC-ROC of 0.697 versus Orthus's retained 0.672. The original selector F1 values 0.292/0.381/0.386 reappear as Max-F1, alongside separate F1 values 0.135/0.222/0.222; these are not evidence of same-setting deterioration. Most matched earlier benchmark results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem formulation, anomaly-scoring notation, and proxy-performance argmax selection rule remain equivalent. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs. The Max-F1 explanation clarifies an empirical metric rather than adding a mathematical development.

C1.justification: V2 qualifies the introduction's performance claim with 'among the evaluated methods' and explicitly confines the conclusion's selector-performance finding to mTSBench. The central contributions—benchmark scale, joint detection/selection evaluation, and substantial selection gaps—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The new Practical Takeaways section explains selector weaknesses through coarse dataset-level features and recommends caution with top-1 recommendations. Additional discussion interprets domain and anomaly-characteristic dependence. Appendices C/G introduce substantive annotation-quality limitations, dataset-specific concerns, and qualifications about interpreting detector agreement, substantially expanding v1's narrower limitations.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents the top-7.5% anomaly-score threshold, clarifies use of official splits and the fallback anomaly-free training segment, and specifies that semi-supervised detector runtimes include training and inference. It also replaces the front-page repository link with a project-site address. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified settings.

R1.justification: V2 adds Wu and Keogh (2023) when discussing benchmark flaws, removes Orion/Sintel from Table 1 and the references, and explicitly distinguishes its multivariate benchmark from the already-cited univariate selection study by Sylligardos et al. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 revises the abstract and local wording, corrects several dataset descriptions, and adds a Practical Takeaways section. Broader Impact moves from Appendix F into the main text, and appendices are reorganized around the new case studies. Most existing exposition and the main narrative sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The paper adopts a substantially different publication template and front matter. Table 2 gains columns and a metric row; Tables 3–5 and Figures 6, C.1, and C.2 introduce new displays. The detector-runtime chart becomes a combined average-bar and dataset-heatmap figure. Several retained figures and tables are also relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important gaps in the benchmark's practical interpretation: Table 2 tests fixed PCA and a simple ensemble against selectors, while the new subgroup analyses and annotation case studies reveal conditions under which aggregate conclusions need qualification. Explicit thresholding and timing details further improve transparency. Section 4.2 incorrectly says Ensemble trails MetaOD, contrary to most Table 2 entries, but this localized error does not outweigh the substantial gains in comparative evidence and limitations.
